title: As Iran’s oil lifeline runs dry, can it outlast Trump's economic siege?
author: Samuel Wendel
text:
Analysis

As Iran’s oil lifeline runs dry, can it outlast Trump's economic siege?

The country's last barrels of crude stockpiled beyond the reach of a US naval blockade fell to zero in October, raising the stakes for Tehran amid mounting economic distress.

Samuel Wendel

This photo taken on Oct. 7, 2026, shows shoppers walking through the Tajrish Bazaar, a traditional market in Tehran. The marketplace in the Iranian capital's north would usually be abuzz with customers, but shops now sit mostly empty with only small numbers of people walking its old narrow paths, a jarring shift for the sellers shouting to promote their goods.
— Atta Kenare / AFP via Getty Images

Iran has reached a grim milestone in its economic confrontation with the Trump administration, with the last barrels of crude stockpiled beyond the reach of a US naval blockade now exhausted.“Iran's oil on water outside the blockade has fallen to zero as of last week, and all volumes have been discharged in China,” Homayoun Falakshahi, head of crude oil analysis at energy intelligence firm Kpler, told Al-Monitor. “This is the first time Iran has faced such a challenge in its modern history.”On paper, Iran’s oil sales reaching rock bottom marks a potential turning point in Washington’s campaign to choke off Tehran’s economic lifelines. But it remains uncertain whether mounting financial pain will force concessions or intensify a conflict as both sides continue saber-rattling.The milestone comes roughly two months into Operation Economic Outcast, a US sanctions campaign backed by a maritime blockade aimed at depriving Iran of revenue to sustain its government and war effort. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted on Sept. 27 that Iran would complete its remaining oil deliveries within two weeks, leaving Tehran with “nothing left to trade for anything.”
